Subject: Draft case study: Quantum Health — review & quote approvals

Hi Kara —

Attached is the first draft of the case study we promised (redwood-quantumhealth-draft-v1.docx). Thank you again for agreeing to participate — this will be used on our website and in a one-pager for sales.

Two specific asks:
1) Fact-check the technical metrics on page 2 (latency and token throughput) — Marcus and Dev copied here to confirm numbers if you prefer we use sanitized ranges vs. exact P99.
2) Quote approval — we pulled a short quote from your product team, but we'd like final sign-off and a version that marketing can use. If you want changes to tone/length, send the edited quote or annotate inline.

Proposed timeline: please return edits/redlines by Fri 27 Feb so we can incorporate and send a final for your legal/marketing sign-off next week.

Attachments: redwood-quantumhealth-draft-v1.docx (track changes welcome)

Thanks —
Monica Patel

redwood.com

From: Kara Simmons <kara@quantumhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Draft case study: Quantum Health — review & quote approvals

Monica —

Thanks for the draft. Attached are our edits (QH-edits-v1.docx) and a few inline comments from marketing. High-level notes:

- We can confirm the customer-facing throughput statement but prefer to remove the precise P99 latency figure. Our external policy is to reference median latencies or ranges.
- Page 3: please remove the exact dataset size reference (HIPAA concerns) — we can provide a redacted statement: "large, de-identified datasets".
- Quote: our VP product suggested a slightly different phrasing that better reflects our risk-averse tone. See comment 12 in the doc.

I can loop in legal/marketing after you incorporate these, but marketing wants to see the revised wording before legal sits on it.

Cheers,
Kara Simmons
Director, Digital Transformation
Quantum Health
kara@quantumhealth.com

Monica / Marcus —

Quick technical confirmation for Kara's team:
- We should avoid publishing single P99 value. Recommend the phrasing: "consistent sub-200ms median response times with P95 latency under 450ms in production workloads" — that keeps useful signal without committing to a single P99 figure that varies by workload.
- Token throughput: we can say "sustained throughput of tens of thousands of tokens per minute for batch inference during peak jobs".
- For the dataset reference, agree with redaction — "de-identified production traces" is safe.

If you want, I can update the draft and push a Google Doc link.

- Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Updated draft & requested quote alternatives

Hi Kara —

Thanks for the edits. I incorporated Dev's suggested safety phrasing and redacted the dataset reference. I pushed the updated draft to Google Docs so your marketing team can comment directly: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2Bq_example_drive_link

Regarding the quote, your VP proposed: "Redwood helped us reduce inference costs and maintain strong service levels across our busiest workflows." Marketing suggested a slightly warmer version; we included both in the doc (short and long). Can you indicate which one is fine for public use, or propose an edit?

Also copying Laura from our comms/legal for visibility — we expect a quick marketing review and then legal sign-off. If legal needs the Word file, happy to send.

Attachments referenced: redwood-quantumhealth-draft-v1.docx (previous version)

Best,
Monica

monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Kara Simmons <kara@quantumhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Quantum Health Marketing <marketing@quantumhealth.com>, Legal <legal@quantumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Updated draft & requested quote alternatives

Monica —

Thanks for moving quickly. Marketing prefers the warmer quote: "Redwood helped us reduce inference costs and maintain strong service levels across our busiest workflows." Legal/comms asked for two minor wording edits:

1) Remove the phrase "reduce inference costs" and replace with "improve inference economics" (internal phrasing requirement).
2) Replace "strong service levels" with "consistent latency and availability" to be explicit.

Proposed final quote (approved by marketing):
"Redwood helped us improve inference economics while maintaining consistent latency and availability across our busiest workflows."

We can sign off on that as soon as Redwood confirms the final doc and removes the dataset size reference. Legal says they don't need a DocuSign for a quote — an email confirmation is sufficient.

Kara
Director, Digital Transformation
Quantum Health
